hypotheses.justification: If R < 0 the set {x : ℂ | ‖x‖ ≤ R} is empty, and TendstoUniformlyOn on the empty set holds trivially (tendstoUniformlyOn_empty). So the statement is true for every R. The proof can do `rcases le_or_gt 0 R`: the case 0 ≤ R is the existing proof, and the case R < 0 is handled by showing the set is empty and applying the trivial lemma. It can be deleted on its own.

δ is a fixed complex number and does not depend on j. On the disk ‖x‖ ≤ R, ‖exp(δx)‖ ≤ exp(‖δ‖R), so the same argument works with the bound B j = 2·τ_j^a·exp(‖δ‖R). This still tends to 0 because a > 0 and τ_j → 0. The factor-norm lemma would be restated with exp(‖δ‖ R), and the lemma's own hδ is only used to get ‖δ‖R ≤ R. The uniform-convergence lemma tendstoUniformlyOn_tprod_one_add_of_tsum_norm_le is applied unchanged. The statement remains true; it can be deleted on its own.

τ_j → 0 gives |τ_j| < 1/2 eventually. For τ_j ≤ 0, ‖(τ_j:ℂ)^t‖ = |τ_j|^t. Also ‖((τ_j^a : ℝ):ℂ)‖ = |τ_j^a| ≤ |τ_j|^a for real rpow with negative base (Real.rpow of a negative number is exp(a log|x|)·cos(aπ)), and for τ_j = 0 it is 0 since a > 0. Hence the same geometric majorant works with |τ_j|^a·exp(R) in place of τ_j^a·exp(R), and B j = 2·|τ_j|^a·exp R → 0 by continuity of rpow. The statement is therefore true without the positivity hypothesis, and the proof only needs the factor lemma stated with |τ| and the bound |τ^a| ≤ |τ|^a. It can be deleted on its own.
